correctness.rationale: An eigenvector with purely imaginary eigenvalue must vanish at the endpoints by the dissipative quadratic form, then vanish everywhere by the nearest-neighbor recurrence with J≠0. Thus e^(−Kt) decays, the integrated Gramian is positive definite, and its Lyapunov solution is unique. The same-parity part G of the Dirichlet inverse commutes with A, since the parity sign conjugates A to −A. The inner-path analogue B commutes on interior rows/columns and is zero on endpoints; hence [A,B] is supported on the boundary, with first-row entries B(2,j) and last-row entries B(N−1,j), matching the skew C anticommutator PC+CP (both vanish between opposite endpoints). For same-parity i<j the four affine neighbor terms in [C,A] cancel before truncation, with missing neighbors at i=1 and j=N contributing N+1−j and i respectively, exactly the corresponding copies of G. Opposite-parity entries there are zero. The commutator diagonal is twice the sum of adjacent C entries, giving −4 in the interior and 2(N−2) at either end. These identities, including N=2 where P=I and Q=I/κ, yield K†Q+QK=I with the stated sign of the imaginary term. The survival expectation is Tr(Qρ); the localized diagonal has the form a/κ+bκ, with a,b>0 in the interior and b=0 at an endpoint. Differentiation and strict convexity give the unique interior optimizer and stated minimum; both limiting optimal rates follow directly. An independent diagonal-phase transformation to a real rational Lyapunov equation followed by exact linear solves checked every complex entry for seven paths N=2 through 8 at varied rational couplings and rates.
residual_risks: The rational samples check normalizations, parities and signs, not the infinite family by themselves. Only equal positive endpoint losses, a uniform coherent path and the total absorption channel are covered; the optimization is for a localized source.

broader_coverage.reasoning: Efficiency with competing mechanisms or a semi-infinite boundary is not the finite two-terminal integrated lifetime. In an equivalent linear stationary covariance formulation the symmetric K gives KQᵀ+QᵀK†=I. Boundary-injection formulas with only boundary-supported noise do not supply the identity forcing at N>2; a general solution covering that forcing could subsume the finding, but no such passage was verified.

equivalent_formulations.reasoning: Adding a second loss changes K on the left and right of the Lyapunov equation, not just its inhomogeneity. Reflection partitions this two-end problem but does not reduce both parts to the cited uniform single-end paths: even N yields a central end detuning ±J after folding; odd N gives a symmetric half with central hopping √2J. The odd antisymmetric half does reduce to a uniform one-sink path but cannot give the whole kernel. The exact single-end optimizer is recovered in the fixed-s limit, not at finite interior s.

value.rationale: The finite coherent path with two terminal absorbers is a natural transport model, and absorption time cannot be recovered from eventual efficiency (which is one). An all-entry formula handles initial relative phases without a matrix solve. The finite-size site dependence of the optimum distinguishes fixed distance from one end from a bulk-scaled start; the exact endpoint case also shows why imposing a universal finite optimal rate would be wrong. This goes beyond solving the routine Lyapunov equation for isolated lengths.
residual_risks: The value is for total mean survival and a localized-source loss-rate choice, not channel-resolved times, a full first-passage law, or an optimum for coherent inputs.
